Why RGLD?
It offers the best overall balance of quality, risk profile, growth optionality, and relative valuation among the group right now.
• Business model advantage: As a pure royalty and streaming company, RGLD delivers high-margin exposure to gold (and some silver/copper) without the operating risks, cost inflation, or capital intensity that miners like Agnico Eagle (AEM) face. Margins routinely sit near or above 80% EBITDA, the cost structure is extremely lean, and cash flow conversion is strong. This is the same attractive model shared by WPM and FNV.
• Track record and shareholder returns: Since the start of 2000 it has delivered roughly 16% annualized total returns—solid long-term compounding. It also has one of the best dividend growth histories in the precious metals sector (25+ consecutive years of increases, ~15% CAGR since 2000, and membership in the S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats). The payout remains well-covered with room to grow.
• Portfolio and growth: The company has meaningfully expanded and diversified through recent acquisitions (including Sandstorm), lengthening reserve life and adding producing and development assets. It still retains embedded growth and optionality from existing streams/royalties while maintaining a strong balance sheet and liquidity for further deals or capital returns (dividends + buybacks).
• Valuation edge: Among the pure royalty/streaming peers, RGLD currently trades at a noticeable discount to both Wheaton (WPM) and Franco-Nevada (FNV) on metrics such as P/E and EV/EBITDA. AEM looks cheaper on absolute multiples, but that discount largely reflects higher operational risk as a traditional miner. RGLD sits in a sweet spot—cheaper than the other high-quality streamers without sacrificing the lower-risk model.
Brief comparison of the alternatives
• WPM: Excellent scale and growth profile, but it often commands the highest premium valuation of the three streamers.
• FNV: Outstanding quality, diversification (including some energy), and consistency, yet it typically trades at a richer multiple.
• AEM: Attractive on pure valuation and a strong gold producer, but it carries the full suite of mining risks (costs, operations, geopolitics) that the royalty model is designed to avoid.
In short, RGLD combines the superior risk-adjusted economics of the royalty/streaming model with a more reasonable entry point than its closest peers and a proven record of compounding returns and rising dividends. That combination makes it my single pick from this group.
